messages.text: Dad, the clinic mailed that senior safety checklist. Do you want me to bring it Sunday and look at the stairs with you and Mom?
Bring it. Rosa says the second rail would help, and I want to fix small things before they become big things.
I can also ask the handyman who did my porch. He does Puyallup jobs and gives written estimates.
Good. We have been here too long to rush into another place over a railing.
Pa, the Hendersons down the street asked if you still patch drywall. Their hallway has two holes from when they moved a dresser.
Tell them I'm not chasing work anymore but I can come look. Two holes is an hour, maybe less. Won't charge for a look.
They said whatever you think is fair. Mrs. H said her cousin still talks about the fence you put up on 14th back in '09.
That fence held. I used cedar posts, not the cheap stuff. Tell her thank you. I'll go by Friday morning with the bucket and the mud.
Pa, I started a new folder for your taxes. The Social Security 1099 came in the mail already?
Si, came last week. That is the only one this year.
Ok good. No W-2, no 1099 from anybody else? I just want to be sure before I open the program.
Nothing else. Just the SSA paper and the bank interest slip from BECU.
I can bring the folding tables Sunday if I get out before the late truck.
Good. Elena said she may come after the phones quiet down.
Tell her 705 is bad coming out of Tacoma at that hour. I will come down from 320th if the dock count closes clean.
Sunday I can come after the warehouse shift. Tell Elena 1:00 works; Luis said he can bring the tablet.
Good. Rosa is counting plates for you three and the small ones.
Mine may be late, around 4. Save two seats if the whole crew is still there.
I will. If all six are running around, the card table goes in the corner.
I can make Sunday if the warehouse shift ends on time. You want me to bring chairs?
Bring two folding ones. Rosa is making the rice the way you three liked it when you were small.
That rice still gets everyone to the table. You need anything else?
Just come when you can. A man does right by showing up, even tired.
Hermano, did you still toast the dried chiles before the big red pot? I found Mama's note with the garlic stain.
Yes, I do it that way. I have hominy soaking and onions from the garden basket.
Good. Rosa said the kids may come by Sunday, so do not use the small pot.
Already pulled the deep one down. I washed the plastic tubs too, just in case.
Pedro, Raul me mando una foto desde Modesto. Dice que todavia tiene la silla verde de Papa en el garaje.
La silla que rechinaba en la cocina? Me acuerdo. Dile que le voy a llamar manana despues del almuerzo.
Si, esa misma. Cuando la vi me acorde de Mama calentando tortillas antes de ir al empaque.
Ay, Tere. Esa parte me pego. Hablamos el viernes con calma, en espanol, como antes.
Dad, the pharmacy line was wild today. Some lady was yelling about the new prescription rules. I just kept my mouth shut and waited.
That is the right move mija. Shouting at the counter never made anyone's blood pressure better. Did Mom's strips come in?
Yes I picked them up. She was going on about how 'they' want to cut Medicare. I don't even know who 'they' is anymore.
That part I do pay attention to. If they touch Medicare or Social Security your mother and I would feel it the same week. Tell her thank you for the strips.
Dad, radar shows light rain until about 8:40 near Pioneer. Want me to check again before you head over?
Yes, please. Ruth already wrote that they will wait by the lobby a few minutes.
Looks clear after 9. Take the dry path by the library, and don't rush the first lap, okay?
I will do the knee stretches first. If it stays clear, I will go.
Dad, I can swing by after I get off Meridian. Bring me the envelope with the W-2s and the folder from last year.
Good. The little program keeps asking about the bank number and I don't want to click the wrong thing.
No clicking ahead. I'll bring my small laptop and we can check the screens together.
Your mother made soup, so come hungry if the drive is not too bad.
I can stop by Sunday after the early shift. Need me to bring the extra folding chairs from Federal Way?
Bring one if Elena comes too. Rosa and I have our usual chairs at the table.
Got it. I will text Elena and Luis so Ma is not setting out more than she needs.
Good. She already planned the smaller pot of beans for before everyone gets here.
Pedro, Sandra posted the new pictures of the baby on her page. Go look when you have a minute.
Okay. I will open it after I finish in the yard. Easier on my eyes when I sit down.
Father Domingo also put the Lenten schedule on the parish page. Stations of the Cross moved to 6 pm Fridays.
Good. I will write it on the calendar so I do not forget.
How did it go with Dr. Nguyen? I saved your coffee.
He said keep watching it. New drops before the next visit, and use the brighter lamp for reading.
Good. I will move the floor lamp back by your chair after lunch.
Thank you. He wants me back in September unless things get worse before then.
Hermano, I found the old envelope with Mamá's notes. She wrote 'remojar hojas temprano' in the corner.
Good. I want that exact line in my own writing so the little ones see how she said it.
And do not forget how she hummed while mixing. The masa always waited for her, not the other way around.
I will put that next to the pork filling notes. Maybe a dicho in the margin too.
How'd it go with Dr. Reyes? Were you there a whole hour?
BP was 138/82. He wants me back in six weeks. Made me redo the whole intake stack, dos páginas de demographics.
Yeah, they split that form last year. You marked the white box on the race part this time? Sometimes new clinics auto-blank it.
Sí, same as always. Y la otra parte la llené también. Copied from the printout you made me bring.
Dad, this is the mower pull-cord clip I mentioned: youtu.be/8Qd-pullcase. Start at 3:10 so you don't have to watch the whole thing.
Gracias. I saved it. The same app showed me a short one from last night's M's game after I opened your link.
That happens. I can set it so the TV opens those clips easier when I stop by Saturday.
Good. I want the repair one on the big screen before I take the cover off.
Pop you see the clip from last night? the stop on south tacoma way
Channel 5 had that thing about the new body cam rule for Pierce County. You see it?
I saw it on the morning news. Your mama and I were talking about it at breakfast. Same conversation we've been having for forty years
Caught the end. Cameras are the right idea. Rules and training too. Without those three together it does not mean much.
couple guys from the warehouse are heading to the thing in front of the courthouse tomorrow at 8pm. you wanna ride with me
Yeah. I still remember walking home from Ramon's that night when I was 16 and they pulled us over by the gas station. You and mom were waiting up.
I have not forgotten that. But when those guys broke into the Garcia's garage last winter we needed someone to come. Both things are true.
No mijo, I'm not driving downtown at that hour anymore. Call me after, I want to hear how it went
Hermano, encontre la libreta vieja de mama. La de las recetas de Tepatitlan que ella trajo cuando se vinieron.
Hermano, encontre una foto vieja en una caja de mama. Tu y yo afuera de la casa en la calle Naches, tenias como siete anos. Salgo arreglando mis manos en el delantal.
Oh Teresa, esa libreta. Mandame fotos cuando puedas, quiero pasarlas al cuaderno que estoy escribiendo a mano.
Mandala cuando puedas. Hace mucho que no veo esa casa. Esa calle siempre olia a manzanas en agosto.
Si. La de birria sale en dos paginas, con la letra de mama. Te acuerdas cuando ella decia que en el rancho de papa la hacian distinto?
Te la mando esta tarde. Tambien hay una de papa con el camion en el lote de la 16th. Yo tenia cuatro y tu cinco creo.
Guardalas bien. Las quiero para el cuaderno de recetas, atras donde estoy poniendo lo de antes.
Como olvidarlo. Mandalas todas hermana, Rosa quiere intentar la de pollo tambien.
I checked the credit union slip. After the pharmacy and the church check, we still have enough for Friday food.
Good. Leave the little drawer bundle alone. I can skip the hardware store this week.
Luis asked again if we wanted him to bring anything.
Tell him just tortillas if he is already stopping. Nothing else.
Dad, I can stop by after lunch and look at the online bill login. Did the password reset email come through?
It came at 12:38 last night. I was already at the desk with the envelopes, so I printed it.
Okay. Also, the number on that card from Dr. Salazar is still saved in your phone if you ever want it.
Leave it there. I am not ready to pay a stranger for family business. Come by for coffee.
I can swing by after the printer thing. Do you need anything from Home Depot while I'm out?
No, mijo. I found screws for the hose reel and the pruning blades are better after a few passes with the file.
Good. Rosa said you two skipped the diner last night too, so I figured you were keeping the errands light.
We ate beans at home. I will also put the old inserts back in my walking shoes before Monday.
Dad, I can swing by after Federal Way and clear the gutters if you still need it.
Yes, thank you. I looked at it from the driveway and left it alone.
Good. Leave the tall stuff for me. Anything else while I am there?
Maybe the garage shelf. I can sort the small boxes on the table first.
Dad, the shop receipt for the alternator is still in my truck. Want me to drop it by Sunday?
Yes, bring it. I left a blank line on the March page for that one.
Got it. That was the one that made February look ugly, right?
Yes. The old total has 3,400 circled, so I want the receipt clipped to it.
I left your little notebook by the coffee tin. Please do it before you pour the first cup.
I saw it. The cuff is still on the chair from yesterday.
Good. I am buying limes and garlic after church calls. We can skip putting the shaker on the table tonight.
Get the darker chiles too. They give the beans enough taste.
Hermano, how is Rosa this morning? Did the cough let her sleep?
A little. I have manzanilla on and caldo started. Elena said call the nurse line if her breathing gets tight or the fever climbs.
Good. A little Vicks, not too much. I will say a prayer for her after breakfast.
Gracias. After she eats I am going to pull the dandelions by the fence before I sit down with the paper.
Dad, I left the library bag by the kitchen chair. The thick one is set in Spain like you asked.
Thank you, mija. That will be better for tonight than those people shouting over each other.
Good. Put on the Mariners recap if you want background noise, not that panel show.
Already changed it. I have my pencil and the page from the Sunday paper.
Dad, I can stop by after lunch and help enter the March numbers in the spreadsheet. Did the pharmacy receipt print clearly this time?
Yes, $18.40 and $11.00 are easy to read. I put them with the power bill and the house policy notice.
Good. Keep the county envelope separate too. I will make the rows lock so you do not move the wrong line again, viejo.
Gracias. Leave the grocery row loose. The others are the ones I do not touch.
You need me to swing by Tuesday, or are you at that Meridian room again?
Tuesday morning I have the loose-hinge table and then Mr. Kwon's cabinet door on the way home.
Got it. Text if the cabinet needs a second pair of hands.
Thanks. It is only two hours there, maybe twenty minutes at his place.
After breakfast, can you cut a little cilantro for the soup? Only a handful.
Yes. I will do it before it gets bright on that side.
And please do not stay bent over too long like last time. Your knee was bad the whole afternoon.
I know. Just cilantro and a quick look at the small green onions.
I found the little blue cooler in the pantry. It still has the ice packs.
Good. If we pick the Friday Harbor one, we can take egg salad, apples, and coffee instead of buying lunch there.
That sounds better. Look for a clean place close to the dock, nothing fancy.
I will check the Victoria page too, just to see which crossing is easier for us.
Dad, I checked the county page after work. The spring clinic at the senior center is only for people who meet the age chart.
Gracias mija. I saw a loud post saying nobody should go, but I will wait for Dr. Nguyen's answer.
Good. Bring the printout Wednesday and ask the pharmacist about timing with your regular pills.
I put the yellow card in my wallet so they can see what I already had last fall.
Hi Dad. Did your envelope from the county show up yet? Mine came Friday.
Yes mija, came Saturday with the booklet. Your mom and I are going through it slow this time, lots of pages on the road levy.
Don't forget the drop box at the library if you don't want to mail it. I pass it on my way home.
We usually just drop it in the mailbox out front, easier on the knees. Thank you though.
You make it out this morning or was it too wet?
I went. George saved me a chair for coffee after, so I could not disappear.
Good. Just keep your pace, Pop.
I stayed behind the faster ones and used the bench near the fountain for a minute.
Pa, that spice cabinet looks like it came out of a furniture store. Mom showed me when I picked up the soup.
Took my time on the hinges. The old ones were chewed up, screws all crooked.
Frank stop by to look?
He came by Thursday. Said his would have been faster. Sure, but mine closes flush, no gap. He kept opening and closing it like he was checking.
Saw a flyer at the parish hall after morning Mass. Father Mike has someone from the dept coming to talk on the 17th at 2pm. Question and answer after.
Who's putting it on
Father Mike and the seniors group. Coffee and pan dulce after. Should be done by 4.
That's an hour I can do. Put it on the calendar with a question mark and I'll tell Marco about it tonight
You still doing that morning loop by Bradley Lake tomorrow?
Yes. Frank called last night and said no more sitting it out. Howard will be there too.
Good. Take the shorter hill if your knee talks back.
I will. Frank keeps the pace slow when I need it.
Dad, I might get off early Sunday. You need me to bring anything?
If you pass the store, get foil lids. I have beans on tonight and rice tomorrow.
Foil lids for the square pans or the round tubs?
Round tubs. The square pans stay here if everyone sits down to eat.
Dad did you see the thread on that group about the council vote? People are tearing each other apart down there.
I scrolled past it. Half of it sounds made up and the other half is just shouting. Not for me.
Yeah it gets ugly fast.
Come for coffee Saturday and we will talk it through at the table. Better that way.
Dad, Marco said the water heater noise was still happening. Do you want me to split the plumber call with him?
Not yet, mija. I moved $125 from the IRA yesterday and we can cover the visit if it stays small.
Okay, but please tell me before you put it off too long.
I will. First I want the credit union to stay above the line Rosa and I wrote down.
Dad, if you are seeing Dr. Morales Monday, bring the last two weeks from the pad. They always ask for the pattern, not one day.
I have most of them. Missed one morning when Luis came early for the printer.
That is fine. Also try the lime-garlic mix again with the fish. It keeps you from adding the extra shake at the end.
Your mother already hid that shaker behind the flour.
Dad, Sofia's school drop-off is really early tomorrow. Could she bring her pajamas and stay at your place tonight?
Yes. I will tell Rosa to put clean sheets on the couch bed.
Thank you. I will pick her up at 6:25. She already packed the purple toothbrush.
That works. Luis and Marco were here Sunday, so the house is still full of crayons and cups.
Dad, I scanned the old tax folder. First joint return in the pile is from 1974, with the Puyallup rental address.
Good. Keep that one with Rosa's recipe cards and the school pictures.
Got it. Also found my kindergarten photo, Marco in soccer socks, and Elena missing one front tooth.
That is the box I wanted. Papers, work stubs, little faces. It tells the story better than speeches.
You sounded wound up after the insurance letter. Need me to look at it Sunday?
Sunday is fine. I already walked to the mailbox twice and sharpened the loppers. Better than staring at the envelope.
Bring it to dinner. Don't let the news run all evening either.
No, mijo. I turned it off. Rosa and I will do the checkbook after coffee and then the rosary.
I put the Safeway and pharmacy slips in the white envelope by your chair.
Thank you. I will add them after lunch and run the calculator again.
The bank paper came in the mail too. Last two quiet months are marked 2,860 and 2,940 in your notebook.
Good. I want this page to stay close to those numbers if nothing else breaks.
Tere called while you were outside. She said Yakima is windy today and she found one more old picture.
I will call her back after lunch. Did she say if Raul got my voicemail?
She said yes, from California yesterday evening. She told me you two would laugh about the truck story again.
Only Tere remembers that story right. I want to hear it in her words.
Are you staying after lunch today, or coming home before I start the beans?
Staying. Frank brought the little score pad, and Howard said he wants his rematch.
Then eat something with the coffee. You forget when you sit at that table too long.
Please come sit down. You have opened the same Comcast paper three times.
I am just making sure the auto pay did not move before the pension deposit.
We can look in the morning with breakfast. The house is too quiet for all those numbers.
Put the folder by the coffee maker. I will try to leave it alone tonight.
Hermano, did you and Rosa still walk by the lake this morning?
Hermano, can you still read the small print in Mama's recipe notebook? I found the chile verde page.
Send it, but take the photo straight on. The yellow pages and tiny writing are harder for me now.
Only the paved part. I held the rail on the little slope and then we sat a few minutes.
I will put it by the window tomorrow and send a clear one. Tell Rosa hello.
That sounds right. No need to rush. I do better when I keep the same route too.
Gracias. The doctor said brighter light helps, so I am trying that first.
Same here. After breakfast is easier than later in the day.
Hermano, I found the old Vicente Fernandez performance we talked about. The link has the red play button: youtu.be/vf-1978-live.
I opened it after dinner. Rosa said keep it low because the 7:10 game is next.
Hermano, encontre el cassette que tenia mama de Vicente Fernandez en vivo. Lo puse esta tarde y me acorde de papa cantando en la cocina.
You and your evening routine. Send me the song one if you find another with good sound.
Ay Teresa, ese mismo lo busque el ano pasado. Pon el lado B, el de Volver Volver con el grito al final. Eso era lo que ponian en la fiesta de tio Beto.
Si! Y los trompetistas, no hay nada igual hoy. Le voy a pedir a mi nieto que lo pase a la computadora para mandartelo.
Mandalo. Lo pongo en el carro los viernes cuando Rosa y yo vamos al mercado. Gracias hermana.
Do you want me to pick up the Costco pack of chicken on my way from Tacoma?
Maybe the small tray. Rosa and I cannot finish the big one before Sunday.
Small tray makes sense. I will bring fruit for the grandkids when we come over.
Thank you. Rosa saved the blue bowls for them.
Dad, did Dr. Kim's office call back about the new estimate?
They did. I told them June is better. I can be careful chewing until then.
Okay, but do not push the small white refill again. The counter said it is ready today.
That one I am picking up before Mass tomorrow. The other office can wait.
You want me to grab those new clippers from Costco? I pass it after work.
Leave them. The old pair is cutting clean again after I tightened the pivot.
Okay. Sunday still at the house or are we doing the Mexican place?
At the house. Rosa has chicken thawing, and I am saving my shoe money for now.
Luis called. He said leave the printer on and do not unplug the little black box beside it.
I only moved the papers. The program still shows the review page.
He said he can come after lunch since he is already nearby for that service call.
Good. I want him to see the forms before we send anything.
Father Acosta called. The sacristy door is dragging again and the trim by the side entrance came loose.
Tell him I'll bring the planer and a couple of finish nails Saturday after Mass. Door is probably the hinge dropped a quarter inch.
He wanted to know what to put in the envelope this time.
Nothing. Same as last year. He knows me twenty years, that's enough. If he insists tell him to put it in the food pantry.
Hermano, Cousin Marta sent another photo from Tepatitlan. The plaza looks the same, only brighter.
I saved it in the Mexico folder. I keep adding pages, then the air fare total makes me close the computer.
Take your time. Ask Elena before you promise anything with that much walking.
Yes. For now Rosa and I are looking at the ferry pages again.
Dad, the nurse at the clinic asked again if you want the visit notes printed in Spanish or English. I told her you read both fine but you prefer Spanish for the medicine instructions. Was that right?
Yes mija, Spanish for the pill instructions. The English on those papers is too small and the words run together. Tu mama is the same.
Got it. I'll mark the chart. Also Sofia wants to know if abuelo can help her with her Spanish homework Sunday, she has a worksheet about grandparents and where they were born.
Claro que si. Dile que traiga la tarea el domingo y le cuento de tus abuelos, donde nacieron y como se vinieron.
Dad, I can come by after lunch. Still need me to move those soil bags?
Yes, please. I already did the tomato row early and that was enough.
Leave the heavy stuff. I will bring the bags around back and set them by the pepper starts.
Good. My knee is quiet right now and I want to keep it that way.
Dad, I can scan the old cards Sunday if you want. Phone camera is fine, but the printer scanner will catch Mamá's pencil marks better.
Bring it. I still want to copy the important ones myself, but a scan helps when my hand gets tired.
Got it. Also Mia asked what 'barriga llena, corazón contento' means after dinner.
Good, I will write that one near the tamal notes so she asks again.
You still going to that thing at the senior center? My buddy sent me a video saying skip it.
I am going after breakfast. The clinic nurse and the paper from the county say I am on the list.
Okay. You want me to drive you or is Mom going?
Rosa will come. We stop at Safeway after so the pharmacist can mark the card right.
Please ask Elena if that paper from the doctor needs a signature or only initials.
I will ask when she is done with the front window.
And Marco said he cannot answer until break. They have a short crew on the floor again.
I remember. I will wait and call both later.
Hermano, did you finish the book with the soldier coming home after the war?
Almost. I stopped when the television repeated that motel story again.
Ay, turn that off. Mama used to say the same bad story twice is no good for the heart.
I did. I worked three little boxes on the back page and made coffee.
Hermano, do you remember the year papa took you out of Davis to help him with the route? I was telling my granddaughter.
It was the spring after tenth grade. I never went back for eleventh. Mama cried but we needed the hands.
I told her you were 16 already swinging a hammer with papa. She thinks kids today have it easy.
Tell her I never had a diploma in my pocket, only callouses. And we ate every night, gracias a Dios.
Hermano, mañana es el aniversario de Papá. Voy a la misa de las 8 aquí en Yakima.
Lo sé, hermana. Rosa y yo vamos a la de las 9:30 en español en St. Andrew's. Le prendo una vela por él y por Mamá.
Llené el papeleo del centro de mayores ayer. La parte de origen me hizo pensar en cómo Papá y Mamá subieron desde Sonora con casi nada.
Yo igual cuando llené lo de la clínica nueva el jueves. Marqué lo mismo de siempre en esa línea. Abuela nos enseñó a no olvidar de dónde venimos.
Hey Pa, Frank texted me a photo of a wobbly chair he's fixing. Said he's going to show you 'how it's done'.
Ha. Tell him the joints have to be clamped overnight or they pop in a week. I'll bring my clamps Saturday.
He said you always say that lol
Because I'm right. We'll see whose chair is still solid by Christmas.
I scanned the county receipt. Want it named 2026_house_tax.pdf or something shorter?
That name is fine. Put it with the 2018 papers and the insurance file, please.
Done. Also, Mom said do not forget the porch-light timer before the handyman comes Wednesday.
I will set it out. If he gives a fair price, the rail and porch light both get done this month.
Pop, did you see what KOMO ran on the Puyallup road bond? They interviewed the woman from the senior center.
Saw the segment on the 5 o'clock last night. KNKX did a piece on it too in the morning. The pamphlet writeup makes it sound smaller than it is.
Yeah the pro and con statements in the booklet were short.
That's why I read both. Your mom keeps me honest on the senior services one. Roads and schools too, those hit us here.
Dad my brother in law was at the house earlier going off again. Said anyone who doesn't pick a side is part of the problem.
I have heard that one for fifty years. From both directions.
He kept pushing me on it. I told him I vote how I vote and I don't owe anybody a yard sign.
Good. Your mother and I never put one up either. I look at the people, I look at what they say about health care and the workers, and I mark the ballot. That is the whole thing.
Pa, the guy who runs the loading dock asked where you learned to weld. Told him you were doing it before I was born.
Started on an old Chevy at sixteen out in the orchards. Tio Beto showed me. By twenty four I was hauling the toolbox over the pass looking for steadier hours.
Snoqualmie in winter with that truck. Mom always tells the story about you driving in over the snow.
Two pairs of gloves and a thermos. Got a framing job in Auburn the first week. Never went back to packing fruit.
Sofia called. The girls at her high school are doing a class debate about the sheriff's office. She wants to know what abuelo would say.
Tell her I would say not everyone gets treated the same way at the stop sign. She should write that down.
She also asked if you would tell her to get rid of them. I told her she should call you.
No. When the Garcia's garage was hit we called 911. Both things sit together. She can write that part too.
Pedro, Elena pregunta si vamos a hacer la ofrenda otra vez en noviembre. Quiere traer la foto nueva de tu mama y la de mi papa.
Si, igual que el ano pasado. Pon en la lista: copal, las veladoras de vidrio largas, y el pan de la panaderia en Tacoma. Las cempasuchil las siembro yo en mayo como siempre.
Bueno. Y dile a Luis que baje las cajas del garaje cuando venga el sabado. Ahi esta el mantel bordado de tu mama.
Le digo. Tambien que arregle el portarretratos de papa, se solto el vidrio.
Ma said your phone made the grocery app freeze. Want me to check it when I come by?
Yes. It would not open the store flyer. I wanted to see if thighs are marked down before Friday.
I can bring the flyer screenshot. Anything else on the list?
Eggs, tortillas, more dry beans, and those small containers if they still have the 12-pack.
Pa, the union hall sent me a letter about the retiree fund for warehouse guys. Got me thinking, did you ever sign up for anything like that back in the day?
No mijo. The jobs I took, customers paid me in cash or a check at the door. Nobody put me on a list anywhere.
Damn. So just the SSA check now?
Just that and what tu mama gets. Forty years of fixing peoples roofs and there is no fund waiting for me. We are okay though.
You need anything from Federal Way on Sunday? I can bring the Costco coffee.
Coffee yes. No more receipts, your mother says. I keep stacking them by the lamp.
Ma told me you were still at the table after 11. Let Luis do the spreadsheet if it keeps going like that.
Luis can fix passwords. The rest stays with us. Your abuelo did not carry house matters to outsiders.
Pa, kid at the warehouse asked if I knew anyone who could redo a bathroom faucet and paint a small room. Won't pay much, single mom.
Send me her address. Faucet is forty-five minutes if it's a standard valve. Paint depends on the room. Tell her I bring my own drop cloths.
She said her uncle paid a guy four hundred to fix a leak and it leaked again two weeks later.
Then he didn't fix it. I charge for the part and an honest hour. If it leaks again I come back, no second charge. That's how it works.
Hermano, Lupita put the photos from Mama's birthday memorial on her page. Did you find them?
Si, Rosa showed me last night. I saved the one of all of us at the cemetery.
Some primos started arguing in the comments about who paid for the flowers. I closed it.
Mejor asi. When you come up in July we sit down and talk about everything in person, not on the phone screen.
Dad, are you still going to the 4th St room tomorrow? I can bring those extra masks by tonight if you want them.
Yes, just 9 to noon. They asked for garden beds again, and Mrs. Lopez gave me two letters she wants read in Spanish.
I will drop them off after work. Please eat before you go.
Hermano, I may come Saturday instead of Friday. Is the front room still okay?
Yes, Rosa put clean sheets there yesterday. We moved the sewing basket off the dresser.
Perfect. I do not need much, just a quiet corner and coffee with you both.
Coffee will be ready. Rosa says bring the Yakima recipe if you find it.
Hermano, I found the picture from the hall in Yakima. Rosa has flowers in her hair and you look too serious.
Send it to Elena, please. The kids laugh at that suit every time.
I will. Mamá wrote 1973 on the back, very neat.
She always wanted the dates right. I only hope the young ones remember we kept coming home after long days.
Ya estas despierto todavia? I was looking at the photo from Naches Road, the one with all of us by the ditch.
Si, aqui estoy. Raul should see that one too. He always says California made him forget the dust.
Mandasela manana. Tonight just tell me if you remember Papa whistling that song.
Claro que si. I can hear it when you bring it up.
Dad did you see the body cam piece from the council meeting? Daniel brought it up last night, he wanted to know what abuelo thinks

Marco sent me the article last week. I told him the same thing I'll tell Daniel - I'll talk about it at the kitchen table all afternoon, but I'm not driving downtown after dark to stand in a crowd at my age
Ha, nobody's asking you to. The library on south hill is doing a panel next Wednesday at 1:30 if you want something quieter. Free and close.
Send me the flyer. South hill in the afternoon is something I can actually do
I am leaving after the last copay batch. If traffic by the Tacoma Mall is still red, I may be closer to 6:40.
That is fine. Marco said he is waiting on one more pallet count.
He should take 18 if he is coming from the 320th side. Rosa asked me to bring the thermometer, so remind me.
I fixed the duplicate PDF. It was saving one copy to Downloads and one to the desktop.
Thank you, mijo. Rosa and I saw the green check but did not know if that meant finished.
Finished after we print the confirmation page. I'll be over in about 20, just leaving South Hill.
I will keep the folder open on the kitchen table.
Dad, I can make your phone text bigger when I stop by Sunday. Want me to do Rosa's too?
Mine for sure. At night the screen looks washed out unless I turn the brightness way up.
No problem. I will set bigger text and reduce the glare setting. Nothing fancy.
Thanks, mijo. Dr. Nguyen said small fixes are enough for now.
Dad someone sent you a fundraising text from a campaign. Want me to block the number? They got your cell somehow.
Block it. I don't send money to any of them. I have gotten two from one side and three from the other this week alone.
Ha. Equal opportunity blocker.
Mostly. The ones talking about immigration like it's a poker game I block the fastest. Real families, Luis. Real workers. Not a slogan.
The kids can come by after Mass. If you are doing the kitchen notebook, Sofia wants to draw the corn husks.
Tell her yes, but she has to listen to the Yakima story while she draws.
Fair. Mateo is bringing his little speaker again, so choose the songs before he picks only cartoons.
I have the old ranchera ready for the page with the husks and masa.
Saw on the Tacoma news a deputy got 30 days for that traffic stop. About time.
Good. If there is no penalty the training does not stick. Same as the office, mija — write-ups have to mean something.
Marco said you were thinking about that night when he was a kid again.
Some things you carry. Does not mean I want to throw the whole thing out. The right answer is the four pieces together.
Dad, did you see that old Hawks goal-line clip I sent? Still makes me mad.
I watched it twice. Then the same screen gave me the spring box score clips from Peoria.
Figures. I might come by next Sunday if the warehouse schedule settles.
Come after lunch. We can put one on while Rosa finishes the rice.
After Mass, can you bring down the fire box? I want the bank letter and the photo from the day we signed the last page.
Yes. That picture still makes me stand taller.
Me too. Eight years already. I will put it back before the grandchildren arrive.
Keep it on the table a little while. They should know why we take care of this place.
The county text came in. They got mine. Did yours come through?
Yes, mine showed received this morning. Good, that's done.
I'm glad we read the senior services one twice. The pamphlet wording was confusing.
Roads section too. They buried the bridge repair on page nine. Next time we start with that one.
Father Ruiz wants the parish anniversary book to list how long families have been in the parish. He asked about us.
Tell him we joined St Andrew in seventy four, right after we moved up here. Before that I was at Holy Family with mama and Teresa.
Fifty two years at St Andrew next month. He will like that. Should I say where you were baptized?
Yes, Holy Family on Chestnut. My mother walked there from our house on Naches.
Do your knees before you leave. The floor is dry by the back door.
I am doing them now. If the clouds hold, I will meet them at nine.
Take the blue jacket. Ruth called here because she did not see your message.
Tell her I am coming, just taking my time.
I fixed the shared photo album. You should see folders from Elena, Marco, and me now.
I see them. Rosa asked why there are six school-picture folders but only three parent folders.
Because we all upload too many pictures, jefe. I put Sofia's folder under Elena's so it is easier to find.
Good. Keep it that way. Her pajama picture from the couch bed made Rosa laugh.
I'll stop by after work for the printer. Want me to bring anything?
Maybe ginger and carrots. Rosa's stomach was off, so I made tea and kept the caldo plain.
Got it. Did you call Elena or should I ask her?
I sent her the numbers already. I am watering the front beds now, then coffee with your mother before I open that printer box.
Pop, pulled up the county voter info update on my tablet. Two screens - race question first, then origin question on its own page.
Mark them the same as 2024, hijo. Don't make me come over.
Looking at the 2024 file now. Origin page you picked the dropdown option with 'Mexican' in the label. Want me to submit the same?
Sí, igual. Y la primera pantalla deja la misma como la última vez. Gracias, hijo.
Buenos dias, hermano. Did you already sit with that arm machine, or did coffee win again?
Machine first today. I wrote both lines down before Rosa came into the kitchen.
Good. For the caldo, roast the chile on the burner and squeeze lime at the end. Mama did that when she wanted flavor without so much from the blue box.
I remember. Garlic too. Rosa says that is why the pot still tastes right.
Hermano, do you remember the shelves you built for mama in the pantry in '78? I'm looking at them now. Still straight.
Pine boards from the Yakima lumberyard, the one by the railroad tracks. I sanded them on the back porch. I was twenty-five and didn't even own a level, I used a marble.
Forty-eight years and not one nail loose. That's why people called you. Even after you moved away the neighbors here still ask.
I never put my name on anything. Just did the job clean and didn't pad the bill. That was the whole trick, hermana.
Dad, the community center has the chair class at 9:30 on Tuesdays, but the hallway walk is open every morning.
The hallway walk sounds better. Flat floor, no surprise steps.
Good choice. Wear the shoes with the wider toe box and take your time.
I will. I can do twenty minutes if I start slow.
Pa, the genealogy site dad's cousin set up wants a city for everyone. What do I put for you and Tia Teresa?
Same one for both of us. The hospital on Tieton, the old building before they rebuilt it.
Got it. And for current city Puyallup since 74?
Closer to seventy six we bought the house. We rented in Sumner the first two years while I was finding work.
Apa, te hice una lista en YouTube como pediste. Le puse los de Pedro Infante, Javier Solis, y unos del Mariachi Vargas que encontre en discos viejos. Te mando el enlace al telefono.
Gracias mijo. Tambien busca el Ave Maria que canta el coro de la basilica de Guadalupe, el que pusieron cuando fuimos en 2008. Rosa lo quiere oir el domingo despues de misa.
Lo encuentro. Una cosa, el bocina vieja del comedor ya no sirve. Te llevo una nueva el sabado cuando pase, asi se oye bien para los dos.
Bueno, traela. Y ensename otra vez como pasar de una cancion a otra sin que se pare. La semana pasada se me apago a la mitad de la del Mariachi Mexico.
Dad your phone keeps pinging because that page from St. Anne's tags you every week. Want me to turn off those alerts?
Leave the parish one and the family ones. Those are the only reasons I open it.
Got it. I will mute the rest of the groups, including that political one Tio added you to.
Please. I do not want to read people fight all day. If Tio wants to know what I think he can come for menudo Sunday.

Dad, the kid's school is doing a heritage thing in April. They want me to bring something from where the family came from. I told her abuelos came from the ranch country outside Tepa but I forgot the rancho name.
El rancho era San Jose, cerca de Capilla. Tu abuelo crecio ahi y tu abuela en el pueblo. Yo naci aqui ya, en Yakima, pero ellos siempre nos hablaban del rancho.
Right. I keep mixing it up because Tia Teresa says it different. I'll tell her teacher. She also asked what language we spoke at home growing up, said she wants to put it on the poster.
Pues espanol, mijo. Hasta la escuela no oi ingles de verdad. Tu mama igual. Dile a la nina que ponga las dos cosas en el cartel.
How was the meeting at Pioneer Park the other week? Mom said you went.
Decent turnout. I asked about written stops policy and the camera retention rule. Chief answered the second one.
Bet some folks there wanted to defund the whole thing.
A few. I do not go that far, m'ijo. When somebody breaks into your shop you still want somebody to come. But the stop you and the boys had on Stewart Street should never have happened either.
I put soup on the stove. Did Sam say your arm could be sore again?
Yes, only today maybe. He said the county sheet matched what Dr. Nguyen wrote.
Good. Elena called and said ignore that scary message from your cousin's feed.
I deleted it. I keep the papers in the kitchen drawer with the yellow card.
Frank called the house. He says his chair held up and yours probably did too.
Probably. Tell him I said the tenons came out clean. No glue squeeze on the show side.
Mijo. Just tell him good job.
I will. But the tenons did come out clean.
Hermano, are you keeping busy today or resting at home?
Going out after noon. Howard said the window table fills up fast, and Frank is bringing the old red deck.
Good. I like hearing you are going again. Bring Rosa one of those oatmeal cookies if they have them.
I will if Frank does not buy the last one first.
Hermano, did you watch any of that thing on the news last night? Everyone in Yakima is fighting about it.
I turned it off after ten minutes. All shouting, no listening. Rosa and I went to bed.
Primo Hector says you should pick a side already, that fence sitters are why nothing changes.
Tell Hector I have been picking my side at the ballot box since Carter. Mine just doesn't have a bumper sticker. I want Social Security to still be there when his mother needs it. That is my side.
Dad, if you and Mom do Victoria or one of the islands, please pick a place where you do not have stairs.
I marked two small places near the ferry. We would bring our own breakfast things and rest after walking.
That is better than trying to rush a big itinerary. Bring the medication list if you are away overnight.
I will. The Guadalajara pages can wait in the folder a little longer.
Dad, the kids have soccer until 5:15 Saturday. We can still stop by after if that is not too late.
Come after. I will keep tortillas warm and the green sauce separate for the little ones.
Do you want me to bring anything from Tacoma?
No, just bring the empty containers from last time. I have soup started with the garden carrots.
Mom said you were limping a little after working by the tomato stakes. Are you icing it tonight?
A little ice, yes. I stopped earlier today, before the heat hit the fence.
Good. Tomorrow just pick what you need for breakfast salsa and leave the digging alone.
Only chilies and cilantro, I promise.
I can stop by after work and pay that online bill for you if the website is acting up.
Come show me, but do not use your card. The SSA deposit and the $100 IRA piece put March at about $3,226.
Got it. I will just bring the laptop and a receipt folder.
Gracias. I also put $40 back in the bedroom tin after Rosa found the cheaper chicken.
Can you tell Elena I found the box of masks she asked about? They were in receiving.
I will tell her. She said their supply cabinet was empty again this morning.
I can drop them after I clock out. Need to stop by the Federal Way branch first and sign off on returns.
Thank you. She will be glad, and Rosa can save a trip.
You watching the late highlights or did Mom take the remote?
Highlights only. The other channel started with three people yelling, so I went back to my book.
Good call. Anything good in that one?
A family crossing the plains. Slow start, but I also have the folded page from yesterday to finish.
I am leaving the green folder on the table. The water bill, house card, and county slip are inside.
I saw it. I will add the Rite Aid receipt after breakfast and we can decide about the clinic estimate tonight.
Please take the morning ones before you go. We can make soup and skip buying meat this week.
Done. I will pick up yours too when the counter opens.
Hermano, Rosa told me you were at the table with the little machine and all those papers again.
Only finishing the March page. Receipts on one side, bank paper on the other.
Better than February then? She said the car made that page jump.
Yes. This one is closer to the old marks, 2,800 and 3,000.
Hermano, I saw little tomato starts at the Yakima store and thought of your yard.
Hermano, Rosa said you were tired after the morning group. Too much standing?
They can wait. I cleaned the old tray and Rosa found seeds in the coffee can.
Only three hours. We did pruners and screws, then I fixed Mrs. Ito's latch before coming home.
Good. For Mateo's birthday, do you want me to mail the card with yours?
Siempre ayudando. Rest your back tonight, please.
I will. Next week is lighter, maybe just one morning.
Yes, just the card. I used polish on my walking shoes, so I can keep them decent for Mass.
I printed the photo labels for tomorrow: 1973, first house, Elena, Marco, Luis, grandkids. Is that enough?
Add Rosa by the stove and the one of my lunch pail. Those belong there too.
Done. Mom said to leave space on the table for the album Teresa mailed.
Good. When they look, I want them to see that the door stayed open and the work was clean.
Dad, I saved Teresa's Yakima number and Raul's California number in your favorites like you asked.
Thank you. Put Tere first if the phone lets you. Hers is the one I use when the old stories come back.
Done. I also labeled Raul's as mobile so you do not tap the old landline by mistake.
I put the black pen and the clean dish towel by your chair. Please do not lean on the masa page while it dries.
Thank you. I am adding your note about soaking the hojas the night before.
Good. Add the part your mother said in Spanish when everyone tried to hurry her.
I remember. I want the grandkids to hear it when we make these together.
